text: #700, step 2 of #599's plan, recorded at #714's merge. Refines D-0281 and D-0313 and keeps D-0350. The real-checkout budget check judges a sandbox's memory by its working memory: the largest sum of anon and shmem within one memory.stat sample. One sampler inside the container takes those samples every 0.1 s for the container's whole life, and it never adds maxima from different moments. The check fails at or above memory.max, on any oom or oom_kill, on process exhaustion, and when counters or sampling evidence are missing or malformed. Reclaimable file cache filling the cgroup no longer fails it: #599's control reached a 512 MiB peak with 128 KiB of anon memory and no OOM. The kernel's memory.peak and memory.events max stay in the report as diagnostics. The host keeps one identified report per container through exit, failure, cancellation and forced removal. The runner marks when the prepare, build, test and accept phases start, and keeps each test's measured elapsed_seconds. So reports give memory, CPU and wall time by phase, and the slowest tests. The four-CPU default, eight workers, 4 GiB and 1,024-process caps, the deadlines and both waves are unchanged. The merger's run on #714's head passed. Working memory was 1.11 to 1.29 GiB, the kernel peak 1.72 to 1.93 GiB, and there was no OOM. The two-sandbox wave took 18m38s to 18m45s and the three-sandbox wave 18m06s to 18m57s, with the factory's planners competing for part of each.
